mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES has risen for four consecutive weeks (4.7 to 7.1), indicating a steady return to in-person work routines that generates incidental shopping and dining trips, which should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose each of the last 3 weeks from 4.7 to 7.1
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES continuing its upward trajectory, indicating decoupling of commute activity from retail footfall.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week jump in PARKS mobility of more than 4 points signals a seasonal/weather-driven surge in outdoor activity that spills over into nearby retail and recreation visits within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 4 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -7.6 to -2.6 (5.0 point jump) in the most recent week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC shows no increase or declines over the next 2 weeks despite PARKS recording a greater than 4 point weekly jump.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous upward movement in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicates that commuting behavior is reinforcing itself through transit capacity utilization, and this joint rise compounds to drive stronger retail footfall growth than either series would predict alone.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rose at t-0w (7.1 and 2.1 respectively)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next 2 weeks is no larger than what WORKPLACES alone would predict, indicating no interaction effect between commuting and transit series.
